reason: My mom is early-stage and still herself, and a camera on her chest that I can open whenever I want feels like watching her, not caring for her. I would rather she have a say in it, and an AirTag in her purse already tells me where she is for a fraction of the cost.
objection: Live video of a parent with dementia, opened from my phone two hours away, is a dignity and consent problem. She would not understand why it is on her, and I would be the one deciding when to look.
would_change_my_mind: If she could understand it and agree to it, the camera only switched on when she pressed the SOS button, and a doctor or dementia specialist told me it helps her and does not upset her.
